newsitem.title: USA: RTRS - Coors says wins row with Molson.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Coors says wins row with Molson.

text.p: Adolph Coors Co said on Sunday a Canadian arbitration panel ruled that Molson Breweries, a unit of Molson Cos Ltd, relinquished all rights to brew and distribute Coors products in 1993 when Miller Brewing Co, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, bought an ownership interest in the Canadian brewer.
Adolph Coors, the holding company for Coors Brewing Co, said the decision was reached late on Friday in Toronto.
Molson Breweries is about 40 percent owned by Fosters Brewing Group Ltd.
The three-member panel found that Molson breached its licensing agreement with Coors by allowing Miller to acquire a 20 percent equity interest in Molson without Coors' consent.

The ruling returns all Canadian rights to Coors products to Coors and requires Molson to pay Coors all of Molson's profits derived from the sale of Coors products since April 2, 1993. The panel also ruled that Molson had committed other breaches that may entitle Coors to damages.
The next phase of the arbitration process -- which is not yet scheduled but could begin early next year -- will determine the full amount of monetary damages due to Coors.
"Coors believes that the amount of damages is significant, although it can't be determined until the next phase of arbitration is completed, possibly in the first half of 1997," the statement said.
According to Molson, the Coors brands represent about eight percent of Molson's total sales volume.

Michael Marranzino, senior vice president and chief international officer at Coors, said Coors cannot make conclusions about the long-term financial impact of the ruling until decisions are made about how best to proceed in Canada.
He said the company believes its future business opportunities in Canada could provide significantly greater financial returns than would have been received under the terminated license arrangement.
"We will be exploring a number of options, including negotiation of a new arrangement with Molson," he said.
In its Friday ruling, the panel also found Molson had underpaid royalties due to Coors from Jan 1, 1991 to April 1, 1993.

Molson made a cash payment to Coors of $5.7 million (net of $600,000 of tax withholdings) during 1996 to cover a portion of the unpaid royalties sought by Coors. In its subsequent financial reports, Coors disclosed the payment, but did not record it as income pending a ruling from the arbitration panel.
The panel agreed that Coors had been underpaid, and the royalty income will now be recorded in the third quarter that ended Sept 29, 1996.
